questions.question: What is the function of transamination?
options: Transfers amino groups from amino acids to α-keto acids
questions.correct_answer: Transfers amino groups from amino acids to α-keto acids
questions.explanation: Transamination transfers amino groups from amino acids to α-keto acids, catalyzed by aminotransferases (ALT, AST).

questions.question: What is the first product of the urea cycle?
questions.explanation: Carbamoyl phosphate is the first product of the urea cycle, formed by carbamoyl phosphate synthetase I from NH4+ and CO2.

questions.question: What is the function of the urea cycle?
questions.explanation: The urea cycle converts toxic ammonia to urea for excretion in the urine.

questions.question: What is the difference between glucogenic and ketogenic amino acids?
questions.explanation: Glucogenic amino acids can be converted to glucose precursors, while ketogenic amino acids are converted to ketone bodies.

questions.question: What is phenylketonuria (PKU)?
questions.explanation: PKU is caused by a deficiency of phenylalanine hydroxylase, leading to accumulation of phenylalanine and mental retardation if untreated.

questions.question: What is the role of glutamate in amino acid metabolism?
questions.explanation: Glutamate serves as the central amino group carrier in amino acid metabolism, accepting and donating amino groups.

questions.question: What is the function of alanine transaminase (ALT)?
questions.explanation: ALT (alanine transaminase) transfers amino groups from alanine to pyruvate and vice versa.

questions.question: What is the clinical significance of elevated ALT and AST?
questions.explanation: Elevated ALT and AST are markers of liver damage or hepatocellular injury, commonly seen in hepatitis or liver disease.
